## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #14148 recall typo matching + whole-word ranking — FEATURE GAP (SMALL ~3-4h)

- **What**: Kilocode #14148 "fix(cli): speed up local recall searches and improve match ranking" adds three recall search improvements: (1) Typo matching: when no session contains every query term, detect small typos (single-char edit distance, session titles only) and return partial matches flagged with their missing terms, (2) Whole-word boosting: rank whole-word matches (`\bquery\b` regex) above substring matches (`query` inside `queryString`), (3) Performance: resolve message roles through a covering recall index instead of reading message rows (SQL optimization, not applicable to Alexi's file-based sessions). Alexi has basic recall (`src/tool/tools/recall.ts`, 175 lines) with (1) simple substring matching (line 135: `messageContent.toLowerCase().includes(params.query.toLowerCase())`), (2) density-based relevance (line 37-43: `occurrences / (content.length / 100)`), (3) top-20 result slicing (line 154). No typo tolerance (exact substring only), no partial results (if query term missing, session excluded entirely), no whole-word boosting (substring matches rank identically to whole-word matches). Feature gap: typo matching + whole-word ranking.
- **Why**: Typo matching reduces false negatives when users misspell a query term (e.g. "orchestartor" -> "orchestrator"), and whole-word ranking improves precision (searching "chat" should rank sessions mentioning "chat" above those mentioning "chatGPT" or "merchant"). Both are user-experience improvements for the existing recall tool. Implementation cost is small: Levenshtein distance 1 check (30 lines), whole-word regex boost (10 lines), partial-result flag in response (5 lines). Total ~3-4h.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14148 (Kilocode recall improvements), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/recall.ts (Alexi recall implementation, lines 135-154)
- **Category**: tool (recall, search, ranking, typo tolerance)
- **Size**: SMALL (~3-4h). Add typo matching (Levenshtein distance 1, session titles only), whole-word match boosting (regex `\b${term}\b`), partial-result flag (when no session contains all terms, return best partial matches with missing terms listed).

#### 2. Cline #14125 agent-loop turn retry for transient provider errors — FEATURE GAP (SMALL-MEDIUM ~4h)

- **What**: Cline #14125 "feat(agents): retry transient provider errors and verify execution in yolo mode" adds turn-level retry for transient provider errors: (1) When a model turn fails with a transient error (429, 5xx, OpenRouter "Provider returned error"), re-issue the turn up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s/2s/4s, capped at 15s), (2) Retryability decided by AI SDK `APICallError.isRetryable`, unwraps `RetryError`, walks `AISDKError.cause`, falls back to HTTP status (429/5xx transient, 4xx permanent except 429), (3) Never retry when turn already streamed content/tool-calls (no event to retract deltas, retry would duplicate output), (4) Increase AI SDK `maxRetries` from 2 to 5 for request-start failures (network/5xx before streaming begins). Alexi has `ErrorBackoff` (`src/core/error-backoff.ts`, 287 lines) with identical exponential backoff (max 5 retries, 1s initial, 60s cap, multiplier 2, line 157-162) BUT it is provider-layer only (used in `sapOrchestration.ts`, not in agent loop). Agent loop (`src/agent/index.ts`, 26522 lines) does NOT retry transient provider errors — a single 429 or 5xx from SAP AI Core aborts the agent run. Feature gap: agent-loop turn retry wrapping provider calls.
- **Why**: Transient provider errors (429 rate limits, 5xx overload, network blips) are common in SAP AI Core (especially free-tier deployments, see `FreeTierRateLimitError` in `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts`). Currently a single transient failure aborts the agent run and surfaces to the user as a hard error. Turn-level retry (distinct from `ErrorBackoff` provider retry) would make agent runs resilient to brief outages without user intervention. Implementation cost ~4h: (1) wrap provider calls in agent loop with retry envelope (50 lines), (2) detect retryability (reuse `isRetryableError` from `error-backoff.ts`, 10 lines), (3) never retry when content/tool-calls already emitted (guard on streaming state, 20 lines), (4) exponential backoff (reuse `ErrorBackoff` class, 10 lines). Total ~4h (SMALL-MEDIUM boundary).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14125 (Cline agent turn retry), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/error-backoff.ts (Alexi ErrorBackoff class, lines 149-259), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/agent/index.ts (agent loop, no turn retry)
- **Category**: agent (retry, resilience, error handling, exponential backoff)
- **Size**: SMALL-MEDIUM (~4h). Add turn-level retry to agent loop: wrap provider calls, detect transient errors (reuse `isRetryableError`), exponential backoff (reuse `ErrorBackoff`), never retry when content/tool-calls already emitted, max 3 turn retries (1s/2s/4s, cap 15s).

#### 3. Cline #14116 SSH remote environments — NOT APPLICABLE (LOW priority, out of scope)

- **What**: Cline #14116 "feat(core): add SSH remote environments" adds SSH remote execution: (1) SSH into a remote machine (via node `ssh2` library), (2) run agent tools (bash, read, write, grep) on the remote machine instead of localhost, (3) cleanup on exit (remove temp files, close SSH connection). Config via new `remoteEnvironment` object in Cline settings (hostname, username, privateKeyPath). This is a multi-machine orchestration feature for GUI apps where users want to run agent tools on a dev server / build machine / VM. Alexi does not have SSH remote execution (no `ssh2` dependency, no remote config, all tools run localhost). Documenting as NOT APPLICABLE.
- **Why**: Alexi is a single-machine CLI orchestrator for SAP AI Core. Multi-machine orchestration (SSH into remote, run tools there) is a fundamentally different use case (GUI app with persistent sessions, remote dev servers) that does not fit CLI architecture. CLI users needing remote execution would SSH into the target machine and run `alexi` there locally (standard SSH workflow). Adding SSH remote environments to Alexi CLI would require: (1) SSH transport abstraction (session/connection pooling, credential management, reconnect logic), (2) Remote tool execution layer (serialize/deserialize tool calls over SSH, handle network failures mid-tool), (3) Config surface (`~/.alexi/remotes.json`?), (4) Security review (SSH key handling, remote command injection). This is a LARGE multi-week project, not a tactical feature. Not actionable for research brief.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14116 (Cline SSH remote environments)
- **Category**: N/A (not applicable to CLI single-machine architecture)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Multi-machine orchestration out of scope for Alexi CLI.
